title: Stronger Bounds for Simpira and Generalized Feistel Structures
summary: Several Simpira permutations have indistinguishability proofs, but most stop at two to the sixty-fourth queries; stronger bounds with a better query–round tradeoff remain open.

formal_statement.body: Prove stronger generic indistinguishability-from-random-permutation bounds for Simpira's Feistel-based permutations and other generalized Feistel structures. Existing proofs cover several Simpira permutations, but most available proofs do not go beyond $2^{64}$ queries, while approaching $2^{128}$ queries requires a very large number of rounds. Establish an improved provable query--round tradeoff, subject to the caveat that Simpira with $b=1$ is always an even permutation and can therefore be distinguished from a random permutation with $2^{128}-1$ queries.

scope.domain: Generic random-permutation indistinguishability for Simpira's Feistel-based permutations and generalized Feistel structures.
parameters: Query count: resource level covered by an indistinguishability proof
Round count: construction cost in the desired query–round tradeoff
b: Simpira parameter identifying the exceptional b = 1 case
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove stronger generic indistinguishability bounds with an improved query–round tradeoff for Simpira and other generalized Feistel structures.

progress.summary: The paper explicitly presents stronger security bounds for Simpira and other generalized Feistel structures as an open problem. It notes that most proofs stop at 2^64 queries and that nearing 2^128 queries requires many rounds, subject to the b = 1 parity caveat.
